items.title: Euro FX futures fell below 1.09 to lowest since April.
items.excerpt: Euro FX futures declined sharply to start the week, sliding from a session high near 1.10 to dip below 1.09 before closing around that level. The intraday move below 1.09 marked the lowest print since April, though modest buying emerged off the lows. Renewed expectations for Federal Reserve tightening supported the U.S. dollar, adding downward pressure on the euro. As prices pressed toward year-to-date lows, implied volatility tracked by the CVOL index firmed higher. Positioning data from last week, prior to Monday's selloff, also showed speculators adding to net short positions, bringing bearish positioning to its highest level in more than 10 years.

items.title: Japanese Yen futures post strongest session since October 22.
items.excerpt: Japanese Yen futures recorded their strongest daily percentage gain since Oct. 22, climbing 0.77% to trade near the session high of 63.23 after touching a low of 62.67. The advance put the yen on pace for its first positive week in four, accounting for nearly all of the 0.77% weekly gain. In economic data, Japan's October headline inflation rose to 2.3% year over year from 2.1%, while core inflation printed at 2.2% against expectations of 2.3%. Following the softer core reading, market-implied probability of a 25 bps Bank of Japan rate hike in December eased to 77% from 87%. A pullback in technology and AI equities also prompted safe-haven flows into the yen and the Swiss franc as the U.S. dollar came under pressure.

items.excerpt: Euro FX futures tested year-to-date lows near 1.0950 before recovering late in the session to trade near 1.0975, roughly unchanged on the day. Over the past several weeks, the euro has fallen approximately 2.5% from its early November highs as hawkish Federal Reserve rhetoric supported the U.S. dollar. Meanwhile, the CME Group Volatility Index (CVOL) for the euro remained relatively steady across the past two sessions while holding above weekly lows. Looking ahead to Friday, market participants are focused on the University of Michigan consumer sentiment report and its inflation components, alongside ongoing commentary from Federal Reserve and European Central Bank officials. Market pricing continues to reflect expectations for December rate hikes from both central banks.

items.excerpt: British Pound futures fell for the sixth session in the last seven, dropping 2.13% over that stretch to reach their lowest level in nearly a year. During the session, the contract recorded a high of 1.3210 and a low of 1.3136 before finishing the New York cash session down 0.48%. The downward move followed October UK inflation data that came in below the Bank of England forecast ahead of its Dec. 17 policy decision. Headline CPI rose to 3.6% year over year from 3.5%, trailing the central bank projection of 3.73%, while services inflation held at 3.7% and core inflation remained at 2.8%. UK labor market figures also showed signs of cooling as regular pay growth slowed to 3.5% from 3.7% in the three months through September.
